metadata.title: Jonah
metadata.subtitle: Jonah 1:1 – 4:11 (20 questions)
metadata.description: Questions on the Book of Jonah according to the King James Version (1769).
metadata.author: King James Version (1769)

questions.text: Whither did Jonah seek to flee from the presence of the LORD (Jonah 1:3)?

options.text: Unto Nineveh, on a ship from Joppa
Unto Tarshish, on a ship from Joppa
Unto Egypt, on a ship from Joppa
Unto Babylon, on a ship from Joppa

questions.text: What did the mariners do during the tempest (Jonah 1:5)?

options.text: They rowed hard toward land and called upon their gods for deliverance
They prayed unto the LORD and fasted until the tempest was appeased
They cried every man unto his god, and cast the wares into the sea
They awoke the shipmaster and cut down the sail together with the mast

questions.text: What happened when they cast Jonah forth into the sea (Jonah 1:15-16)?

options.text: The ship sank at once, and the men swam with great peril to the land
The tempest increased exceedingly, and the men were yet more afraid
The mariners took him up again, and the wind ceased from blowing
The sea ceased from her raging, and the men feared the LORD greatly

questions.text: How long was Jonah in the belly of the fish (Jonah 1:17)?

options.text: Three days and three nights
Seven days and seven nights
Twenty days and twenty nights
One whole day and a night

questions.text: How does Jonah describe his affliction in the fish's belly (Jonah 2:6)?

options.text: I wandered in the wilderness, and burning sand covered me completely
I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth was about me
I was compassed with flames, and fire consumed me almost to the death
I fell into a darksome pit, and the rock shut out all breath of life

questions.text: With what words does Jonah conclude his prayer (Jonah 2:9)?

options.text: I will offer thee everlasting sacrifices
Blessed be the name of the LORD
Salvation is of the LORD
The LORD hath afflicted me sore

questions.text: What proclamation did Jonah cry in Nineveh (Jonah 3:4)?

options.text: Nineveh shall fall, and adversaries shall burn her high towers
Repent and weep, or sudden death shall come upon you all
The LORD is full of grace, turn ye every one from evil ways
Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown

questions.text: How did the king of Nineveh react to the word (Jonah 3:6)?

options.text: He arose from his throne, laid his robe from him, and sat in ashes
He caused the prophet to be bound and cast into prison for evil words
He mocked the strange message and commanded his idols to be praised
He gathered all his host of war and prepared for battle at the gates

questions.text: How did God respond to the turning of the people of Nineveh (Jonah 3:10)?

options.text: He punished them nevertheless, because their iniquity was exceeding great
God repented of the evil, that he had said he would do, and did it not
He kept silence and suffered them to perish in anguish and great fear
He demanded greater oblations from the people before he granted pardon

questions.text: Why was Jonah displeased at the sparing of Nineveh (Jonah 4:2)?

options.text: Because he was ashamed that his prophecy concerning Nineveh came not to pass
Because he feared to lose his reputation and honour among all holy prophets
Because he knew that God is gracious, merciful, and of great kindness
Because he deemed all his long journey and weary labor to have been in vain

questions.text: What did God prepare for Jonah beside the city (Jonah 4:6-8)?

options.text: A spring of cool water to refresh him, and a gentle wind out of the west
A cave in the rocks against the burning heat, and a dark cloud in heaven
A booth of cypress boughs, and a fruitful tree yielding pleasant shadow
A gourd to be a shadow, and then a worm and a vehement east wind

questions.text: With what question does the Book of Jonah conclude (Jonah 4:11)?

options.text: Should not I spare Nineveh, that great city of more than 120,000 persons?
Why wilt thou contend with thy Maker, Jonah, and be angry at his mercy?
Thinkest thou that thine anger is just concerning this great heathen city?
Wilt thou be my judge, Jonah, and forbid me to save that which was lost?

questions.text: Put these events from the Book of Jonah in the correct chronological order.

options.text: Jonah prayeth in the belly of the fish
In the tempest the lot falleth on Jonah
Jonah taketh ship at Joppa for Tarshish
The gourd withereth away by the worm
The mariners cast Jonah into the sea

questions.text: How did Jonah identify himself to the mariners (Jonah 1:9)?

options.text: I am an Hebrew; and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven
I am a Syrian, serving the everlasting Maker of heaven
I am a Phoenician, fearing the LORD who created earth
I am a trader from Joppa, following the LORD on the sea

questions.text: Where was Jonah during the great tempest (Jonah 1:5)?

options.text: He stood upon the deck and looked out on the foaming sea
He was gone down into the sides of the ship, and slept
He helped the mariners to lighten the vessel of its wares
He knelt before the shipmaster and prayed for deliverance

questions.text: What counsel did Jonah give to the mariners (Jonah 1:12)?

options.text: They should turn back and row hard to bring the ship to land
They should furl all sails quickly and cast out the rudder
Take me up, and cast me into the sea; so shall it be calm
They should offer a solemn sacrifice and call upon his God

questions.text: Whither did Jonah's prayer come according to Jonah 2:7?

options.text: Unto the high mountain tops towering over the deep
Unto the ears of the mariners upon the tossed vessel
Unto the deep depths beneath the waters of the ocean
Unto the LORD, into his holy temple in the heavens

questions.text: How large was the city of Nineveh according to Jonah 3:3?

options.text: An exceeding great city of three days' journey
An exceeding great city of seven days' journey
An exceeding great city of ten days' journey
An exceeding great city of five days' journey

questions.text: What decree did the king of Nineveh publish for man and beast (Jonah 3:7-8)?

options.text: The cattle should be driven forth out of the city gates into pastures
Let neither taste any thing, nor drink water, but be covered in sackcloth
The beasts should be adorned and offered in sacrifice to ancient gods
Both should drink wine and raise a joyful shout in the market places

questions.text: What did Jonah do on the east side of the city (Jonah 4:5)?

options.text: He built an altar of stones and praised God for saving the citizens
He departed in sorrow and journeyed toward Tarshish to flee again
He made him a booth, and sat under it in shadow, to see what became
He walked through all the streets, crying once more unto repentance
